A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MoGe and contain complete, readable main text and appendices A–D. Corresponding equations, tables, figures, and experimental passages support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original point-map, depth, and camera-FOV evaluations, quantitative ablations, and qualitative reconstructions, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and qualitative reconstructions, revises quantitative results, and reports additional ablation controls.

M1.justification: MoGe retains its affine-invariant point-map representation, encoder-decoder architecture, ROE solver, training losses, and camera-recovery procedure. The newly evaluated alternatives are ablation controls; the proposed method in Section 3 and Appendix A is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 21 training datasets, eight point/depth benchmarks, three FOV benchmarks, and DIV2K/open-domain qualitative examples. The added ablations do not introduce new data coverage or task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds affine-invariant depth prediction and least-squares/L2 alignment as comparison variants. External baseline membership in Tables 1–3 remains unchanged. Table 6 retains GeoWizard but removes its separate indoor, outdoor, and object variant rows; UniDepth's added V1 suffix does not identify a new comparator.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated point-inlier denominator from the ground-truth point norm to the minimum of predicted and ground-truth norms, retaining the 0.25 threshold. Table 4 adds two global-loss-only control configurations. Existing splits, sample counts, and preprocessing descriptions remain unchanged; the evaluation-data correction footnote does not specify what data were repaired.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Table 4 add targeted tests of whether affine-invariant depth can substitute for point-map prediction and whether least-squares/L2 alignment can replace ROE. Existing median-alignment, truncation, local-loss, normal-loss, and infinity-mask analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. FOV means/medians and average benchmark ranks remain descriptive summaries rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2, 4, and 6 revise substantial quantitative evidence. MoGe's KITTI scale-invariant point error changes from 8.62 to 5.47, and DDAD local point error from 1.08 to 6.74. KITTI affine-point error leadership switches from MoGe to UniDepth: 7.69 versus 7.94 becomes 4.86 versus 4.29. Two ablation result rows are added and three GeoWizard variant rows removed. These are corrected/replaced results, not demonstrated model improvements under identical evaluation conditions. FOV results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The point-inlier formula in Section 4.1 receives a non-equivalent mathematical redefinition: normalization uses the smaller predicted/ground-truth norm instead of the ground-truth norm alone. The method's formal assumptions, ROE lemmas, proofs, and derivations in Appendix A remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and scope: affine-invariant point maps, ROE alignment, multi-scale local supervision, and strong zero-shot geometry, depth, and FOV estimation.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 interprets the added affine-depth control's uneven performance as further evidence for the point representation's handling of focal-distance ambiguity, and extends the alignment comparison to L2. The earlier statement that truncation improves training stability disappears. Appendix D's thin-structure and temporal-consistency limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 documents the added affine-depth control's shift/ray outputs and L1 depth/shift plus MSE ray losses, and identifies the analytical least-squares control. Table 4 explicitly marks its first six rows as global-loss-only; v2 specified this for its first three rows. A correction/reproducibility footnote is added, while existing access links and main training details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the 77-work bibliography retain the same cited research and contribution positioning. Changed citation page backlinks reflect text reflow, not added references.

P1.justification: The representation and alignment paragraphs in Section 4.3 are locally rewritten, ablation labels are clarified, and an evaluation-correction footnote is added. Small punctuation and caption edits accompany these changes; the overall narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 4 expands from seven to nine rows and reorganizes its controls. Table 6 removes three GeoWizard subrows and changes spacing and variant markers. Captions and nearby text reflow locally. Figure imagery remains unchanged throughout the main text and appendices.

improvement.justification: The added affine-depth and L2 controls strengthen evidence for the representation and solver. However, substantial score corrections receive only an unspecified data-error explanation, and revised Table 6 introduces a selection inconsistency: v2 selects DA V1's best ETH3D scale-depth error, 8.80, whereas v3 reports 9.41 despite listing an outdoor variant at 8.77 under the same best-variant rule. Together with the removed GeoWizard breakdown, these reporting regressions make the net quality benefit uncertain.
